# Fair cost sharing calculator: Shapley value, nucleolus and core, a shared-road split, and the Talmud rule for claims

> Free online fair cost sharing calculator. Split a shared cost by the Shapley value (Shapley 1953) and the nucleolus (Schmeidler 1969; sequential LPs of Maschler, Peleg & Shapley 1979), with SCRB and ENSC (Young, Okada & Hashimoto 1982), proportional and equal splits beside them, and a core check that names the subgroup each split overcharges most. Road mode: give each household's distance along a shared private road, pipe or runway and each stretch is split among those who use it (Littlechild & Owen 1973). Claims mode: divide an estate that cannot pay every claim by the Talmud rule (= nucleolus; Aumann & Maschler 1985), random arrival (= Shapley value; O'Neill 1982), proportional, constrained equal awards and losses. Checked against an independent scipy implementation on 40 games and against the Mishnah's three estate divisions. Runs in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Free to use and source available (FSL-1.1-MIT). Arithmetic on the numbers you supply, not legal, tax, financial or professional advice. A road agreement, deed, contract, statute or court may require a different split.

## Pages

- [The tool](https://marisstella.app/cost-sharing-calculator/)

## Use it from code

- `node cli.mjs groups.csv [--game cost|value]` (rows: `A+B,170`)
- `node cli.mjs road.csv --mode road [--total 18000]` (rows: `name,distance`)
- `node cli.mjs claims.csv --mode claims --estate 200` (rows: `name,claim`)
- Add `--csv` or `--json` for machine output.
- `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call cost-sharing-calculator analyze --input '{"mode":"claims","csv":"a,100\nb,200\nc,300","estate":200}'`
- From JavaScript: `shapley(c, n)`, `nucleolus(c, n)`, `coreCheck(c, n, x)`, `airportShapley(needs)`, `talmud(claims, estate)`; `c` is an array of costs indexed by bitmask.

## What it answers

- How should neighbours split the cost of maintaining a shared private road or driveway?
- What is each member's Shapley value, and the nucleolus, of this shared cost?
- Would any subgroup pay less by going alone (is the split in the core)?
- Is the core empty, and by how much (the least core)?
- How do you divide an estate or a pot that cannot pay every claim?
